applicable_when: The kernel is a tensor transpose: input has stride (4032000, 1, 32000, 128) and output has stride (4032000, 31500, 250, 1). The load address y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1 means adjacent threads along the x-dimension (XBLOCK=128) access elements separated by 128 floats (512 bytes) in the source tensor — a classic non-coalesced strided read. This causes 0% L1 hit rate and saturates L2 at 96.9%. The fix is to coalesce both the global load and the global store by aligning the fast thread dimension with the stride-1 axis of the source tensor, using a square TILE and @triton.autotune to find the best tile size.
